title: File:Fluorescent light strip 2 tube.JPG
author: Chetvorno
description: A two tube fluorescent light strip in a ceiling. This is one of the most common types of residential light fixtures in the US.  It takes two F40T12, 4-foot long, 1.5 in dia. rapid start fluorescent tubes.  It has a magnetic ballast and consumes roughly 80 watts.  Fixtures of this type are being replaced in new construction with the more efficient T8 and LED fixtures.

title: File:Sharp Optonica SA-2121H receiver dial lighting 01.jpg
author: Retired electrician
description: Sharp Optonica SA-2121H receiver (Euro market, made in 1978) on the bench. Needed just a small repair in protection relay circuit, otherwise fully functional after 40 years. Here is the lighting for the radio dial (underexposed to reveal 'the secret'). Six fuze-shaped lightbulbs illuminate the edge of a long, angled plexiglass bar which serves as a lightguide. Most light is lost in transit, but a small fraction reaches the other edge of the bar, producing very even, diffused lighting of the dial.

title: File:Skylight in the abandoned City Hall Station (32155).jpg

description: The defunct City Hall subway station in New York City, closed since 1945. The station has several skylights. Most of them are built into the arches above the platform. This is the sole circular skylight above the mezzanine. Visible from above in the middle of the City Hall parking lot.

title: File:Electric Airbus Beluga.jpg
author: Michael Weinold
description: There are efforts to electrify commercial aircraft. Obviously, most of these are focused around the use of high-energy-density batteries. However, all these projects are focusing on general aviation aircraft or "air taxis". Using batteries to power long-haul aircraft is currently not possible. For comparison, see the recent "EUROCONTROL Think Paper #21 - Long-haul flight decarbonisation: When can cutting-edge energies & technologies make a difference?" This is what makes this image an excellent humorous illustration of any materials related to either electric aircraft specifically, or sustainable aviation in general.
